Elon Musk claims that Ukraine allegedly violated Starlink's terms of use and used the system on combat drones.

As someone who was inside the process at the Ministry of Defense, I can say with certainty that this is not true.

In February of this year, whitelists were introduced. Stationary terminals could be registered by both military personnel and civilians.
But for any satellite terminal to work while on the move, it had to be added to a special list and connected to the military Starshield system. Otherwise, no satellite communication terminals in Ukraine would work.

In other words, using civilian Starlink for drone missions was technically impossible. All drone missions that required satellite communication could only be carried out using Starshield.

We are very grateful to the United States and SpaceX for access to critically important satellite communications. Ukraine did not violate the terms of use.

items.tx:
I just had a very disturbing conversation with a young man in the sauna at my local gym. 

After exchanging some basic pleasantries, the conversation quickly moved to his family roots in Qatar. He told me about his father being mistreated there, despite "building much of the country's infrastructure." Without prompting, he made several remarks regarding the state of the Middle East, and before I knew it, we were talking about Israel. 

He explained to me that global terrorism, and especially terrorism in Israel, was natural. "It's because people are trying to break out of prisons," he said. "Gaza is a concentration camp." While I repeatedly disagreed with him in a polite and measured tone, he grew more and more excited. "The only sovereign nation in the Middle East is Iran!" he told me. "How's that working out for them?" I asked. He also explained to me that "Israel has killed more children than any other country." I asked him about the horrific deaths of children in other wars, to which he had no answer. I asked him about Hamas using the people of Gaza as human shields. He refuted that, as well, suggesting that Hamas wouldn't harm children. 

He then went on to explain that eventually, the Jews will be outnumbered — and that in time — Israel will be overrun and undone. He seemed exhilarated by the thought of it. "It's getting too hot in here," he said — before abruptly leaving. I just stood there stunned. By all accounts, a normal, probably well-educated young man in Canada, defending terrorism, celebrating the strength of the Iranian regime, and openly predicting Israel's destruction. 

As I got changed and headed home, I couldn't stop thinking about our talk. There was no green bandana or inverted red triangle — but it was clear how he felt about the situation. How he viewed the world. There are thousands and thousands of young people like this here in Canada, and throughout the West — and in time — we're going to pay a civilizational cost for not addressing this problem when we had the chance.

🚨MAJOR BREAKING: The Rothschild dynasty has been handed the keys to Ukraine's banking system. 

On Friday, October 23, 2026, Ukraine's Ministry of Finance signed three-party agreements with the state-owned banks Ukrgasbank and Sense Bank and London-based N.M. Rothschild & Sons Limited, part of the Rothschild & Co group. The firm, hired in consortium with Ukrainian investment bank FinPoint, will not buy the banks — it will prepare and run their sale to foreign investors. Ukrgasbank is roughly 95% state-owned; Sense Bank was nationalized from Russian-linked Alfa Group in 2023. Both are profitable, and both sit among Ukraine's ten largest lenders.

It happened this way because the process was engineered from outside. Rothschild was chosen through a competitive tender, but the framework was laid down step by step: the Cabinet approved privatization preparations on October 1, 2025, approved the adviser-selection rules on October 29, 2025, and opened the tender on March 31, 2026. The real spur is Ukraine's repeated commitment to the IMF to engage an adviser for exactly these two banks, with sales slated to begin around 2027. Rothschild's role will be to value the assets, package them for investors, market them abroad and organize the tender.

The beneficiaries are the foreign financial groups that end up buying in, plus Rothschild itself, which earns a fixed fee and a success fee of up to 3% of proceeds either way. Ukraine benefits in the short term by raising budget cash while the hryvnia sits at an all-time low of 45.20/$ and the IMF projects a $50–55bn financing gap for 2027–28 — but it pays for that by offloading income-producing assets during a war, at a moment when it is forced to be a seller rather than a holder.
